files.reason: P2pNcclEngine gathered KV on the idle send_stream while the forward stream's KV write was still queued; gather now runs on the compute stream and send_stream waits on a recorded event. Without this, remote-prefill decode output is garbage. PUT_ASYNC now drains the whole send queue and moves each (remote, dtype) group with one PUTS handshake and one NCCL transfer; per-(request, layer) round trips serialised prefill instances at ~18 rps regardless of prompt length. Batches are capped at 256 MiB and the receiver copies each slice out of the flat buffer: views pinned the whole batch until every request in it had been consumed, which OOMed a D instance under sustained sharegpt load. recv_tensor now pops a slice from recv_store on consumption (freeing the pooled block after the H2D copy); upstream kept every consumed slice until the request finished, a second copy of each D request's prefill KV that grew with concurrency and OOMed the receiver regardless of kv_buffer_size.

kv_both support: the leg of a request (send KV / load KV / plain) is decided per request from ___decode_addr_ in its id versus this engine's own ZMQ address instead of from the fixed kv_role, so one instance can be relabelled P, D or M at runtime. Save and load metadata are kept in separate lists. Scheduler side remembers decode legs whose KV was already scheduled for loading, so a preempted request recomputes its prefill locally instead of waiting for a slice the engine has released.
